identity.name: Sheikhdom of Qatar
alt_names: Qatar under Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim

land.text: Qatar, which 'the Ottomans had incorporated ... into their dominion' by January 1872 as a province in Najd, and over which they 'officially renounced sovereignty ... in 1913'

predecessors.note: The Ottoman dossier credits the 1913 loss of Qatar's cells to emirate-of-nejd (Cliopatria's year); the History of Qatar page has the Ottomans renouncing their claim, not Nejd taking the land. The same Al Thani house ruled the peninsula before 1872 (qatar-dynasty, Wikidata Q846).

land.text: the Qatar peninsula, which 'became a British protectorate on 3 November 1916 when the United Kingdom signed a treaty with Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim Al Thani'

successors.note: qatar-protectorate is a Cliopatria row (1947-1955) written by another part of me-10; its shapes are the Omani polygon, not Qatar's. Its dossier should start in November 1916; the independent State of Qatar follows on 3 September 1971 (slug state-of-qatar, Cliopatria row from 1973).

capitals.name: Doha (Al Bidda)
capitals.note: The History page: 'Doha developed around the largest of these, Al Bidda'; the Ottoman garrison 'lives in the fort of Al Bida''. The Qatar page gives Doha as the capital; neither page states a capital for 1913-1916 in words.

keyframe_review.note: 12.8 k km2 (15 cells) for 1913-1914: the whole Qatar peninsula (Natural Earth 'Qatar'). The Qatar infobox gives 11,581 km2 for the modern country, a ratio of 1.10 for the Cliopatria area. The History page names no other land for the sheikhdom in 1913 (Zubarah remained a Bahraini-claimed place until the 2001 ICJ award, which the page mentions; the shape holds it).

correction.text: the Qatar peninsula unchanged, with the years extended through 1916 (to the treaty of 3 November 1916)

keyframe_review.note: Same polygon as 1913 (12.8 k km2). The shape should run to 3 November 1916, when Qatar 'became a British protectorate' (Qatar page), although the Cliopatria row ends in 1915; the Ottoman garrison left Doha's fort in 1915 'with the presence of British gunboats in the harbour'.

ledger.note: 1913: the Ottomans renounce sovereignty over Qatar and Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim Al Thani rules the peninsula. 'The Ottomans officially renounced sovereignty over Qatar in 1913'; a 1915 British description quoted on the page has 'Shaikh Abdullah, who succeeded to the chiefship of Qatar in 1913'; the Qatar page: 'By the Anglo-Ottoman Convention of 1913, the Ottomans agreed to renounce their claim to Qatar'. A garrison of 'at the most, 100 infantry' stayed in the Al Bidda fort until 1915.

region.text: Doha's fort (Al Bidda), the garrison's last post

ledger.note: 1915: the last Ottoman garrison leaves Doha. 'In 1915, with the presence of British gunboats in the harbour,' Abdullah bin Jassim persuaded the remaining garrison to leave Doha's fort, which British troops found deserted.

3 November 1916: Qatar becomes a British protectorate. 'Qatar became a British protectorate on 3 November 1916 when the United Kingdom signed a treaty with Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim Al Thani'; the British protection is a vassal event for the British dossier, and the sheikhdom continues as qatar-protectorate until independence on 3 September 1971.

certainty.note: The peninsula's coast is a natural frontier; its land border with the mainland is not fixed by any page opened (the History page has Percy Cox draw a line separating the peninsula from the mainland only at the 1922 Uqair conference, after this dossier's years).

sources.title: History of Qatar
sources.note: 1913 Ottoman renunciation, Abdullah bin Jassim in 1913, the Ottoman garrison at Al Bidda, the 1893 Al Wajbah battle, the 1922 Uqair line; no area.

sources.title: Qatar
sources.note: Infobox area 11,581 km2; the Anglo-Ottoman Convention of 1913, the 1915 withdrawal from Doha's fort, the protectorate of 3 November 1916, independence 3 September 1971.

notes: Two pages opened (History of Qatar, Qatar) against a budget of 1-2. Same state or not: Wikidata Q846 is shared with qatar-dynasty (1820-1904 in Cliopatria; the existing dossier ends in January 1872 with the Ottoman province) and state-of-qatar (1973-2024). They are the Al Thani sheikhdom under successive names, interrupted by the Ottoman province of 1872-1913; this dossier keeps to the Cliopatria 'Qatar' years 1913-1915 plus 1916 to the British treaty and does not merge the rows, because the colour registry and the other parts already treat them as separate slugs. GAP for the orchestrator: no row and no dossier covers the Qatar peninsula between the 1916 protectorate and 1971 except Cliopatria's 'Qatar Protectorate' (slug qatar-protectorate, 1947-1955), whose two shapes are the Omani polygon (307,787 km2, bbox 52.1-59.9 E, 16.7-26.4 N), not Qatar's; the Muscat and Oman rows carry the Qatar cells in 1916-1935. The qatar-protectorate dossier (another part) should be written from 3 November 1916 to 3 September 1971 on the Qatar peninsula, or this dossier extended. Not settled: Abdullah bin Jassim's reign dates (the pages give 1913 for his accession and no end), so no rulers strip; the extent of Zubarah and Khor Al Adaid (the History page: 'Abu Dhabi-occupied Khor Al Adaid in 1882'); the Ottoman garrison's date of withdrawal ('cusp of Ottoman withdrawal ... in 1915'; the Qatar page puts it in 1915 with British gunboats) against 'In 1913 Turkey consented to remove her garrison'. The History page does not give the day of the 1916 treaty; the Qatar page does. No war within the life of this dossier (the 1893 Battle of Al Wajbah is earlier and belongs to the Ottoman province years).
